newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy moves to ban most night flights.
newsitem.headline: Italy moves to ban most night flights.

text.p: The Italian government on Wednesday approved a decree barring night flights at most of the nation's airports, in an effort to make the skies a little less noisy.

The decree will prevent all commercial airplanes from taking off or landing between 11.0 p.m. and 6.0 a.m. starting in June 1998. The ban does not include the intercontinental airports of Rome Fiumicino, Milan Malpensa and Bergamo.
The measures, signed by the environment and transport ministries, need the final go-ahead from local authorities.

They will affect some 50 international and national flights in the airports of Bologna and Venezia in Northern Italy, Bari and Olbia in the South and Palermo and Catania in Sicily, the Environment Ministry said.
Medical, emergency and postal flights will not be included and some exceptions will also be made for particularly silent planes whose noise level does not surpass 60 decibels, the decree said.

"With these measures, we are able to safeguard citizens' health, which is put at risk by the high decibels that go hand in hand with an expanding transport system," said the undersecretary at the environment ministry, Valerio Calzolaio.
